items.answer: Yes, with clarifications applied. notchCalculator('BBB+','BB+') -> {notches:3, direction:'downgrade', wl:2}; ('BBB+','BBB-') -> {notches:2, wl:1}; 1-notch downgrade -> calculator wl 0 (C6); countryRatingChangeWl 1 notch -> 1, 2+ -> 2; upgrades/unchanged -> 0 (C3); 'bbb+' = 'BBB+'; other input -> RangeError (C1). The POC example (2 notches, WL=1) is not test data; C2 replaces it.
items.quote: BBB+ → BB+ = 3-notch downgrade → WL=2, and BBB+ → BBB- = 2 notches → WL=1

items.answer: (1) The REQ-06-02 example miscounts: BBB+ -> BB+ is 3 notches; C2 resolves: WL=2. (2) Calculator WL uses Indicator 13 thresholds, country indicator uses Indicator 12 thresholds (C2, C6), so the same pair can differ (BBB+ -> BBB: calculator 0, country 1). (3) 'Pre-filled from public source' is out of scope (C4). (4) 'Editable' met by input params (C7). (5) 'Displayed' met by return value (C8). Meaning of 'trimmed' is open: X-input-trim.

items.answer: Both requirements are Must; partial delivery is not useful. Order: RATING_SCALE and notchChange first, then notchCalculator and countryRatingChangeWl (built on notchChange).

src/ratings/notch.mjs: RATING_SCALE = 19 C1 strings in order ([0]='AAA', [7]='BBB+', [18]='CCC-'); notchChange(previous,current) = index(current) - index(previous), integer -18..18, positive = downgrade; notchCalculator returns {notches (same signed value, C5), direction 'downgrade'|'upgrade'|'unchanged', wl: 2 if notches>=3, 1 if notches=2, else 0}. src/indicators/countryRating.mjs: countryRatingChangeWl(previous,current) = 2 if notchChange>=2, 1 if ==1, else 0. Inputs are rating strings, case-insensitive; invalid -> RangeError.
items.quote: `notchChange(previous, current)` → integer; positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged.

items.answer: notchChange, notchCalculator and countryRatingChangeWl throw RangeError when previous or current is not one of the 19 scale entries after trimming/case-folding (includes '', whitespace-only, 'BB B', 'Baa1', 'CC', 'D', 'NR', null, undefined, numbers, objects). No fallback, no partial result, no logging.

items.question: C1 says the input is 'trimmed' but does not say which characters are removed. Which leading and trailing characters must be stripped before a rating is matched? Are look-alike characters (Unicode minus U+2212 or en dash in 'BBB−', fullwidth letters) normalised or rejected?
options: A: JavaScript String.prototype.trim(): all Unicode whitespace and line terminators (incl. NBSP U+00A0); look-alikes rejected
B: ASCII whitespace only (space, \t, \n, \r, \v, \f); NBSP and other Unicode spaces rejected; look-alikes rejected
C: spaces only (U+0020); everything else rejected
D: A plus look-alike normalisation (U+2212 or en dash -> '-', fullwidth -> ASCII)
items.impact: Changes observable behaviour: ('BBB+\u00A0','BBB+') returns 0 under A or D but throws RangeError under B or C; 'BBB−' (U+2212) accepted only under D. Tests and QA data cannot be fixed until answered.

history.question: C1 says the input is 'trimmed' but does not say which characters are removed. Which leading and trailing characters must be stripped before a rating is matched? Are look-alike characters (Unicode minus U+2212 or en dash in 'BBB−', fullwidth letters) normalised or rejected?

items.answer: Trimmed means String.prototype.trim(): leading and trailing whitespace of any kind (spaces, tabs, newlines, Unicode spaces such as NBSP) is removed; whitespace inside the value is not changed.
